headline: Amazon's first profitable year
text: Amazon reported net income of $35 million for 2003, its first profitable year, against a loss of $149 million in 2002. Fourth-quarter net income was $73 million.
imageCaption: Jeff Bezos at the Web 2.0 conference, San Francisco, October 2004

headline: eBay raises its forecast to $3 billion
text: eBay reported record fourth-quarter revenue of $648 million, up 57%, and 2003 revenue of $2.17 billion, up 78%, with net income of $442 million. It raised its 2004 revenue forecast to $3 billion.

headline: ExxonMobil's profit nearly doubles to 21.5 billion
text: ExxonMobil said on 29 January that it earned 21.51 billion dollars in 2003, up from 11.46 billion in 2002. The total includes one-off gains, among them a 2.23 billion dollar US tax settlement in the fourth quarter; without them, profit was 17.03 billion.
source: ExxonMobil press release of 29 January 2004 (Form 8-K exhibit 99.1), https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/34088/000003408804000018/r012904ex991.htm (read 2026-10-03); ExxonMobil press release of 31 January 2005 (names the 2.23 billion tax settlement in 4Q03), https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/34088/000003408805000026/r013105ex991.htm (read 2026-10-03)

headline: Federer wins in Melbourne and becomes world number one
text: Roger Federer won the Australian Open on 1 February, beating Marat Safin in the final, and with it became the world's number one tennis player for the first time. It is his second Grand Slam title after Wimbledon last July. He is 22.

headline: Shareholders rebuke Eisner; Comcast bid rejected
text: At Disney's annual meeting 43% of the votes cast were withheld from Michael Eisner, and the board took the chairman's title away from him while keeping him as chief executive. The protest was led by Roy E. Disney and Stanley Gold, who quit the board last year. Earlier this year the cable company Comcast made an unsolicited offer for Disney worth about 54 billion dollars, which Disney's board rejected.

headline: Google offers free e-mail with a whole gigabyte
text: On 1 April Google launched Gmail, a free e-mail service with one gigabyte of storage per user, a significantly higher amount than competitors offer.

headline: Nokia loses market share and warns
text: On 6 April Nokia said first-quarter sales fell 2% to 6.6 billion euros instead of rising 3-7%, as its handset volumes grew 19% in a market that grew more than 25%; its ADR fell more than 15% before trading opened. On 16 April it confirmed its market share had fallen to about 35% and warned of second-quarter earnings well below last year's.
imageCaption: The Nokia N-Gage game phone, launched in October 2003

headline: Boeing launches the 7E7 Dreamliner
text: On 26 April Boeing's board approved the 7E7 Dreamliner, a new mid-size long-range jet made largely of carbon composites, after All Nippon Airways ordered 50, worth about 6 billion dollars. It is the largest launch order for a new Boeing jet, with first deliveries planned for 2008.
imageCaption: The Boeing 787 Dreamliner (called the 7E7 until January 2005), shown at its 2007 unveiling in Everett

headline: Recovery in the numbers, trouble in the chips
text: On 13 April Intel reported first-quarter revenue of 8.1 billion dollars, up 20% from a year earlier, and net income up 89%, as companies spend more on computers again. It is moving production to a 90-nanometre process, and it settled a patent case with Intergraph for 225 million dollars.

headline: Jim Cantalupo dies suddenly
text: McDonald's chairman and chief executive Jim Cantalupo died of an apparent heart attack on 19 April in Orlando, at the company's worldwide franchisee convention, aged 60. President Charlie Bell, an Australian who started at a Sydney McDonald's at 15, was named chief executive. Sales have been rising since the 'I'm lovin' it' campaign of September 2003.
imageCredit: McDonald's Corporation (non-free image on English Wikipedia)

headline: No more money for Mitsubishi
text: On 22 April the boards of DaimlerChrysler decided at an extraordinary meeting not to take part in a new capital increase for Mitsubishi Motors, which is in trouble after a quality scandal. DaimlerChrysler is pulling back from its Asian alliance; in May it also restructured its alliance with Hyundai.
source: Mercedes-Benz Classic, Illustrated Chronicle 2004 ('DaimlerChrysler withdraws from Mitsubishi Motors', 22 April 2004; Hyundai, 12 May and 16 August 2004), https://mercedes-benz-publicarchive.com/marsClassic/en/instance/ko/2004.xhtml?oid=4913323 (read 2026-10-03); https://www.encyclopedia.com/social-sciences-and-law/economics-business-and-labor/businesses-and-occupations/daimler-ag (2000 Mitsubishi stake, read 2026-10-03)

headline: UBS fined 100 million dollars over banknotes sent to Iran and others
text: On 10 May the US Federal Reserve fined UBS 100 million dollars for sending US banknotes to Cuba, Libya, Iran and Yugoslavia, countries under US sanctions, from a dollar depot it ran in Zurich for the New York Fed. The Fed says employees hid the deals by falsifying monthly reports. The Fed ended the contract in October 2003.

headline: Ten countries join the EU
text: On 1 May the European Union grew from 15 to 25 members: Poland, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Slovakia, Slovenia, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Cyprus and Malta. Seven of them were in the Soviet bloc fifteen years ago. Switzerland must now decide whether to extend the free movement of people to the new members.
imageCaption: Signing of the accession treaty of the ten new member states, Athens, 16 April 2003

headline: BMW opens its first car plant in China
text: BMW and its Chinese partner Brilliance officially opened a new car plant in Shenyang in northern China in May. BMW is also having a record year: it has launched the X3, the 6 Series and new 5 Series models and will launch a compact car, the 1 Series, in September.
source: BMW Group Annual Report 2004 (Shenyang plant officially opened in May 2004; model launches), https://bib.kuleuven.be/files/ebib/jaarverslagen/BMW_2004.pdf (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BMW (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: A BMW 5 Series (E60) with a Chinese number plate, built in China

headline: Citigroup pays $2.65 billion over WorldCom
text: Citigroup agreed to pay $2.65 billion before tax ($1.64 billion after tax) to settle the class action of WorldCom investors over the shares and bonds it sold for the company. It is taking an after-tax charge of $4.95 billion in the second quarter, which also covers its remaining exposure to Enron and other litigation.

headline: NBC Universal is born; Genworth is spun off
text: General Electric combined NBC with Vivendi's Universal film and TV business into NBC Universal, of which GE owns 80%. It also completed the spin-off of most of its mortgage and life insurance business as Genworth Financial.

headline: Neville Isdell called back to run Coca-Cola
text: On 4 May Coca-Cola named E. Neville Isdell chairman and chief executive elect, to succeed Douglas Daft by early summer. Isdell, an Irish citizen who grew up in Africa, spent decades at Coca-Cola opening new markets before leaving in 1998 to head a big bottler, and retired in 2001. The board had looked at several outsiders.

headline: Judge allows sex-discrimination suit for 1.6 million women
text: A federal judge in San Francisco has certified a class action against Wal-Mart on behalf of about 1.6 million women who have worked in its US stores since late 1998. They claim they were paid and promoted less than men. Wal-Mart denies it and will appeal.

headline: Coal price doubles in six months
text: Australian thermal coal averaged about $60 a tonne in June, against $34 in December, as Chinese and other Asian power stations compete for supply; copper is trading near $2,700, up from $2,200. For the world's largest exporter of thermal coal, every dollar on the coal price drops straight to profit.
source: World Bank Commodity Price Data (Pink Sheet), monthly averages, CMO-Historical-Data-Monthly.xlsx updated 2026-10-02; Xstrata circular 2 Feb 2009, https://www.rns-pdf.londonstockexchange.com/rns/6630M_-2009-2-2.pdf (both read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Aerial view of the Mount Owen coal mine complex, New South Wales, Australia

headline: Mack leaves; Grübel runs Credit Suisse alone
text: John Mack left Credit Suisse at the end of his three-year contract in early July; Oswald Grübel, with the bank for more than 30 years, is now sole chief executive of the group. Brady Dougan becomes head of Credit Suisse First Boston and Walter Berchtold head of the Swiss bank.
source: Credit Suisse Group Form 20-F for 2004, filed 30 March 2005, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1159510/000102123105000251/b78781x20-f.htm (read 2026-10-03)

headline: A 3-dollar special dividend and a 30 billion dollar buyback
text: Microsoft's board approved a one-time special dividend of 3 dollars a share, a quarterly dividend of 8 cents, and plans to buy back up to 30 billion dollars of its own shares over four years. The company had accumulated more cash than it could use.
imageCredit: Kees de Vos from The Hague, The Netherlands

headline: Google goes public at 85 dollars
text: Google, the most used search engine, sold shares at 85 dollars on 19 August, raising 1.67 billion dollars and valuing the company at more than 23 billion.
imageCaption: Larry Page, with Eric Schmidt behind him, at the Nasdaq MarketSite as Google's shares start trading, New York, 19 August 2004

headline: Cisco grows again, with sales of $22 billion
text: Cisco reported fiscal-year sales of $22.0 billion, up 16.8%, and net income of $4.4 billion. Sales in the quarter to July rose 26% from a year earlier to $5.9 billion.
imageCredit: World Economic Forum from Cologny, Switzerland

headline: Two million iPods in a quarter
text: On 13 October Apple reported a profit of 106 million dollars on sales of 2.35 billion for the quarter to September, sales up 37%. It shipped 2,016,000 iPods, five times as many as a year earlier, its retail stores' sales grew 95%, and it expects a much better December quarter.
imageCaption: "iPod, Therefore I Am": Steve Jobs with an iPod on the cover of Newsweek, 26 July 2004
imageCredit: Newsweek cover (as printed by Cult of Mac)

headline: Oil passes $55 on Chinese demand
text: US crude reached a record $56.37 a barrel on 26 October, up from about $33 in January. China's oil use is growing about 8% a year, OPEC has little spare capacity, and attacks on Iraqi pipelines continue. Earlier in the year, when oil reached $40, European finance ministers cut their growth forecasts.

headline: Greece's deficits were bigger than reported
text: On 22 November Eurostat, the EU's statistics office, published a report on Greece's budget figures, after an audit launched by the government elected in March. The deficit for 1999, the year on which Greece's entry into the euro was judged, was 3.4 percent of economic output, not 1.8 percent, and so above the 3 percent limit; for 2003 it was 4.6 percent instead of 1.7 percent. Military spending had been under-recorded and the surpluses of the social security funds overstated. Greece keeps the euro, but the reliability of its statistics is now openly questioned.
source: Eurostat, Report on the revision of the Greek government deficit and debt figures, 22 November 2004, https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/documents/4187653/5765001/GREECE-EN.PDF (read 2026-10-04); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Greek_financial_audit (read 2026-10-04)

headline: Bush re-elected after a campaign fought over Iraq
text: George W. Bush won a second term on 2 November with 286 electoral votes to John Kerry's 251 and 50.7% of the vote; Ohio decided it. Kerry argued that Bush had misled the country into the Iraq war, where no banned weapons had been found; Bush voters named terrorism and traditional values as what mattered most to them.

headline: Isdell lowers Coca-Cola's long-term growth targets
text: After warning in September that second-half results would fall short, Coca-Cola on 11 November cut its long-term targets to volume growth of 3 to 4% a year, operating income growth of 6 to 8% and earnings per share growth in the high single digits. It will spend 350 to 400 million dollars more each year on marketing and innovation, and expects weak results in some key markets to continue into 2005.
source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/21344/000002134404000183/ko8k1111x99-1.txt (press release of 11 November 2004, read 2026-10-03); https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/21344/000002134404000138/ko8k9150499-1.txt (warning of 15 September 2004, read 2026-10-03)
imageCredit: World Economic Forum from Cologny, Switzerland

headline: Charlie Bell steps down; Jim Skinner takes over
text: On 22 November Charlie Bell stepped down as chief executive to fight colon cancer, diagnosed soon after he took over in April. Vice chairman Jim Skinner, a 33-year McDonald's veteran, became chief executive, and Mike Roberts, head of McDonald's USA, president. The US business is heading for a second year of double-digit operating income growth.
imageCredit: Rob LaRosa from Las Vegas, NV, USA

headline: Altria considers breaking itself up
text: On 4 November chairman Louis Camilleri told investors that Altria's tobacco businesses are significantly undervalued compared with other tobacco companies, and that Altria is looking at separating into two or three independent companies, preparing to act 'when the litigation environment permits'. He expects 2004 earnings at the top of the guided range of 4.55 to 4.60 dollars a share. Altria shares gained about 19% in November.
source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/764180/000115752304010378/a4758835ex99.txt (Altria press release of 4 November 2004, read 2026-10-03); month change from data/out/mo.json

headline: 2004 in review: steady gains as the Fed starts raising rates
text: The S&P 500 gained 9% in 2004 to 1,211.92 and the Dow 3.2%. The Federal Reserve began raising its key rate on 30 June, in quarter-point steps from 1 to 2.25 percent by December, as the recovery gathered strength.

headline: IBM sells its PC business to China's Lenovo
text: On 7 December IBM agreed to sell its personal computer division, including the ThinkPad laptops, to the Chinese computer maker Lenovo for 1.25 billion dollars in cash and stock, with Lenovo also taking on 0.5 billion dollars of liabilities. Lenovo will move its headquarters to New York.
imageCaption: A ThinkPad notebook, the line IBM sold to Lenovo

headline: Lehman's profit jumps 39% to a record
text: Lehman Brothers' net income rose 39% to a record $2.4 billion in the year to November 2004, with a sixth consecutive year of record revenues from bond trading.

headline: Nvidia will design the PlayStation 3's graphics
text: Nvidia announced that it will help Sony design the graphics processor for the PlayStation 3 games console.
